c.st: If AI replaces workers, should it also pay taxes?
c.x: You could tax the energy and subsidize it for individuals. It's the ultimate resource that all business uses. But that would mean unscrupulous countries could tax their energy less and attract AI farms. So probably you need to tax imported tokens (and other goods) as well. There could be many benefits of taxing grid energy instead of labor.

c.st: Sir Humphry Davy’s unpublished poetry found in notebooks
c.x: Richard Holmes wrote a great book called "The Age of Wonder: How the Romantic Generation Discovered the Beauty and Terror of Science" which covers Humphry Davy as well as other late 18th-century/early 19th century figures such as Samuel Taylor Coleridge (who was a friend of Davy's and who was an amateur chemist as well as a professional poet just as Davy was the reverse).

c.st: The 50 Best Nonfiction Books of the Past 25 Years
c.x: I'm pleased to see that one of my favorite books, Richard Holmes' "The Age of Wonder" was there. This is a book that describes how in the 1700s and early 1800s the cultures of science and literature were much more merged than they are today -- you had poets like Wordsworth writing poems about Newton and actually reading the Principia themselves, and you had scientists like Humphrey Davy writing poems.
